notes.text: At the pentecost of Sinai, in the Old Testament, and the pentecost of Jerusalem, in the New, where the two grand manifestations of God, the legal and the evangelical; the one from the mountain, and the other from heaven; the terrible, and the merciful one. They were all with one accord in one place — So here was a conjunction of company, minds, and place; the whole hundred and twenty being present.
And suddenly there came a sound from heaven — So will the Son of man come to judgment. And it filled all the house - That is, all that part of the temple where they were sitting.

And there appeared distinct tongues, as of fire — That is, small flames of fire. This is all which the phrase, tongues of fire, means in the language of the seventy. Yet it might intimate God's touching their tongues as it were (together with their hearts) with Divine fire: his giving them such words as were active and penetrating, even as flaming fire.

And they began to speak with other tongues — The miracle was not in the ears of the hearers, (as some have unaccountably supposed,) but in the mouth of the speakers. And this family praising God together, with the tongues of all the world, was an earnest that the whole world should in due time praise God in their various tongues. As the Spirit gave them utterance - Moses, the type of the law, was of a slow tongue; but the Gospel speaks with a fiery and flaming one.
And there were dwelling in Jerusalem Jews — Gathered from all parts by the peculiar providence of God.
The multitude came together, and were confounded — The motions of their minds were swift and various.
Judea — The dialect of which greatly differed from that of Galilee. Asia - The country strictly so called.
Roman sojourners — Born at Rome, but now living at Jerusalem. These seem to have come to Jerusalem after those who are above mentioned. All of them were partly Jews by birth, and partly proselytes.

Cretans — One island seems to be mentioned for all. The wonderful works of God - Probably those which related to the miracles, death, resurrection, and ascension of Christ, together with the effusion of his Spirit, as a fulfilment of his promises, and the glorious dispensations of Gospel grace.
They were all amazed — All the devout men.

But others mocking — The world begins with mocking, thence proceeds to cavilling, chap. iv, 7; to threats, iv, 17; to imprisoning, chap. v, 18; blows, v, 40; to slaughter, chap. vii, 58. These mockers appear to have been some of the natives of Judea, and inhabitants of Jerusalem, (who understood only the dialect of the country,) by the apostle's immediately directing his discourse to them in the next verse. They are full of sweet wine - So the Greek word properly signifies. There was no new wine so early in the year as pentecost. Thus natural men are wont to ascribe supernatural things to mere natural causes; and many times as impudently and unskilfully as in the present case.

Then Peter standing up — All the gestures, all the words of Peter, show the utmost sobriety; lifted up his voice - With cheerfulness and boldness; and said to them - This discourse has three parts; each of which, ver. 14, 22, 29, begins with the same appellation, men: only to the last part he prefixes with more familiarity the additional word brethren. Men of Judea - That is, ye that are born in Judea. St. Peter spoke in Hebrew, which they all understood.
It is but the third hour of the day — That is, nine in the morning. And on the solemn festivals the Jews rarely ate or drank any thing till noon.
But this is that which was spoken of by the prophet — But there is another and better way of accounting for this. Joel ii, 28

The times of the Messiah are frequently called the last days, the Gospel being the last dispensation of Divine grace. I will pour out of my Spirit — Not on the day of pentecost only, upon all flesh - On persons of every age, sex, and rank. And your young men shall see visions - In young men the outward sense, are most vigourous, and the bodily strength is entire, whereby they are best qualified to sustain the shock which usually attends the visions of God. In old men the internal senses are most vigourous, suited to divine dreams. Not that the old are wholly excluded from the former, nor the young from the latter.
And upon my servants — On those who are literally in a state of servitude.

And I will show prodigies in heaven above, and signs on earth beneath — Great Revelations of grace are usually attended with great judgments on those who reject it. In heaven - Treated of, ver. 20. On earth - Described in this verse. Such signs were those mentioned, ver. 22, before the passion of Christ; which are so mentioned as to include also those at the very time of the passion and resurrection, at the destruction of Jerusalem, and at the end of the world. Terrible indeed were those prodigies in particular which preceded the destruction of Jerusalem: such as the flaming sword hanging over the city, and the fiery comet pointing down upon it for a year; the light that shone upon the temple and the altar in the night, as if it had been noon-day; the opening of the great and heavy gate of the temple without hands; the voice heard from the most holy place, Let us depart hence; the admonition of Jesus the son of Ananus, crying for seven years together, Woe, woe, woe; the vision of contending armies in the air, and of entrenchments thrown up against a city there represented; the terrible thunders and lightnings, and dreadful earthquakes, which every one considered as portending some great evil: all which, through the singular providence of God, are particularly recorded by Josephus. Blood - War and slaughter. Fire - Burnings of houses and towns, involving all in clouds of smoke.

The moon shall be turned into blood — A bloody colour: before the day of the Lord - Eminently the last day; though not excluding any other day or season, wherein the Lord shall manifest his glory, in taking vengeance of his adversaries.

But — whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord - This expression implies the whole of religion, and particularly prayer uttered in faith; shall be saved - From all those plagues; from sin and hell.

glossa.text: *In the same place.* Namely in the upper room, into which they had gone up. He who desires the Spirit treads upon the dwelling-place of the flesh, transcending it by the contemplation of the mind.

*From heaven.* The Spirit is given from heaven, that God may be loved; on earth he is given, that the neighbour may be loved: for twice after the resurrection was he given, for the commending of the two precepts of charity. *A sound.* It may be called the speaking of tongues sounding from the mouth of the apostles. *Spirit.* Before the passion the Spirit was given to the apostles for the grace of teaching and of healings; after the resurrection Jesus breathed the spirit, and said: *Receive the Holy Spirit; whose sins you shall forgive, they are forgiven them ((Joan. XX))*, etc. Which gift he had given to Peter alone beforehand: but, as is believed, then by anticipation, now with the rest by completion it is bestowed on Peter also: and the power of forgiving was given to those whom he was sending to the office of preaching.

*Mighty.* By comparison with what went before, the grace of the apostles is called mighty, or the Spirit came in the likeness of a mighty wind. *The whole house.* The Spirit is poured into them sitting in one house, that the unity of the Church may be commended, the third law beginning in the upper room. At the giving of the law the people stood far off for fear; here, at the coming of the Spirit, they had been gathered into one out of love. *Sitting.* That there might be fulfilled what had been said to them: *Sit you here in the city.* Sitting is a token of humility and of stability: by which a seat is prepared for the Holy Spirit, who rests upon the humble.

 ((GREG.)) The Spirit appeared in fire, but through himself, etc., *as far as* and hearts were taught by the voice or by the sound.

*Parted.* The dispersion of tongues was made at the tower, but what pride dispersed, humility gathers together again: in pride is dispersion, in humility concord is made. Behold, the sentence of the Lord is fulfilled which says: *I will not leave you orphans, but I will send the Paraclete Spirit ((Joan. XIV))*, who, being their advocate, spoke for them in all tongues. He brought tongues, who came for the Word, for the tongue has kinship with the word, so that they cannot be separated from one another. So the Word of the Father, that is the Son, and the Holy Spirit are inseparable, nay rather of one nature. *As of fire.* The same Spirit came in fire: because sinners *the Spirit purges, enlightens, kindles, burns.* For fire has four natures, *it burns, purges, warms, enlightens.* In like manner the Spirit burns up sins, purges hearts, shakes off torpor, illumines ignorances. Fire is incorporeal and invisible in its own nature; but when some body has been assumed it is seen, appearing of diverse colour, on account of the materials in which it burns. So the Spirit will not be able to be seen, save through the creatures in which he works.

*And they began.* Behold the sign of fulness: a full vessel bursts out. Fire cannot be hidden in the bosom. *With divers tongues.* Because they spoke with all tongues, or, speaking in their own, that is the Hebrew tongue, they were so understood by all as if they spoke in the proper tongues of each, according to that of the Prophet: In other tongues and with other lips will I speak to this people, etc.
*Out of every nation,* etc. ((RAB.)) As if it were said: Wheresoever born. But the captivity, which was made under Antiochus not many times before, caused the Jews to be born among all nations.

*Confounded.* That confusion is set over against the confusion of tongues, from which Babel obtained its name. So the humility of the apostles answers to human pride. *Every man.* All the tongues are said to be seventy-two: whence also the disciples of the second order were chosen under this number, that the number of the preachers might accord with the number of the tongues.

*We have heard.* In this it was signified that one Church would speak in the tongues of all nations.

 ((BEDA.)) It is asked whether those who were speaking, etc., *as far as* it seemed rather to be a miracle of the hearers than of the speakers.

*Cappadocia,* etc. These five provinces which are set after Judaea do indeed speak Greek: but from the custom of their country there is a diversity in sound. Whence wonderful was the grace in the apostles, which not only taught them the diversity, but also made in their speech the distance of properties in each of the tongues according to the number of the provinces.
*Strangers of Rome.* In the Greek, sojourning Romans, that is, Jews who led a pilgrim life at Rome.
*Jewish men.* That is, there are two causes of prudence, namely that they were Jews, and that they dwelt in Jerusalem, which sobriety becomes.

*I will pour out.* By this word he shows the largeness of the gift, because the Spirit was to be given not, as of old, to prophets and priests only, but to all persons everywhere in either sex. *Of my Spirit.* He looks to the diverse gifts while he says this, but not to a diminution of the substance. *Upon all flesh.* What all flesh is he consequently expounds there: *And the sons shall prophesy,* etc.

((RAB.)) Upon all flesh, of male and female, or of the circumcised and the heathen, according to that: *There is not male and female, circumcision and uncircumcision, Barbarian and Scythian, bond and free ((Gal. III))*. 

*And they shall prophesy.* The law and the prophets until John: from him the kingdom is preached. But it is one thing to prophesy of Christ, another to foretell and to teach things to come.

*And I will give.* Mystically, wonders in heaven are labours in the Church. Signs, upon the earth. Vengeances, upon the earthly. Blood, in martyrdom. Fire, of the Gospel or of the Holy Spirit. Vapour of smoke, the compunction of the soul or of the heart. *Wonders in heaven.* For indeed at the birth of Christ a new star appeared; at his ascending the cross, the sun was darkened and heaven was overspread with darkness.

*Blood.* Not only of the wound, but also of the sweat, when in prayer his sweat became as drops of blood, which is set among the signs of the Deity, because it is not found in human nature. Therefore it signifies that the whole world is to be washed by the blood of Christ, that as the tabernacle had been consecrated by the blood of victims, so the faithful people might be dedicated by the blood of the same: and that not only at Jerusalem should there be a place of prayer, but that in every place of his dominion the elect should lift up their hands by prayers to the Lord. *Vapour of smoke.* A vapour, namely, of compunction and of weepings. Because as smoke from fire, so compunction from the ardour of the Holy Spirit.

*The sun shall be turned,* etc. This is believed to have been done partly in the passion of Christ, partly to be about to come before the day of judgment. For then the sun was darkened, but the moon turned into blood could not appear to men: because then (as being in the Pasch) standing as the fifteenth, it had by day been hidden from human sight by the interposing of the earth.

notes.text: Creeping — This word is common to all creatures that move without feet.

Leviathan — The whale. Therein - Who being of such a vast strength and absolute dominion in the sea, tumbles in it with great security, and sports himself with other creatures.

20. Darkness - Which succeeds the light by virtue of thy decree.
Hidest — Withdrawest the care of thy providence.

Spirit — That quickening power of God, by which he produces life in the creatures from time to time. For he speaks not here of the first creation, but of the continued production of living creatures. Created - Other living creatures are produced; the word created being taken in its largest sense for the production of things by second causes. Renewest - And thus by thy wise and wonderful providence thou preservest the succession of living creatures.

Rejoice — Thus God advances the glory of his wisdom and power and goodness, in upholding the works of his hands from generation to generation, and he takes pleasure in the preservation of his works, as also in his reflection upon these works of his providence.

He looketh — This is a farther illustration of God's powerful providence: as when he affords his favour to creatures, they live and thrive, so on the contrary, one angry look or touch of his upon the hills or earth, makes them tremble and smoke, as Sinai did when God appeared in it.

Praise ye the Lord — Hebrew. Hallelujah. This is the first time that this word occurs. And it comes in here on occasion of the destruction of the wicked. And the last time it occurs, Rev. xix, 1, 3, 4, 6, it is on a like occasion, the destruction of Babylon. In the former psalm we praise God for his common providence; in this, for his special favours to his church. The first eleven verses of it David delivered to Asaph, (1 Chron. xvi, 7, &c.) to be used in the daily service of the sanctuary. Here is the preface, ver. 1-7. The history itself in several articles: God's covenant with the patriarchs, ver. 8-11. His care of them in a strange land, ver. 12-15. His raising up Joseph, ver. 16-22. The increase of Israel in Egypt, and their deliverance out of it, ver. 23- 38. His care of them in the wilderness, and their settlement in Canaan, ver. 39-45.

glossa.text: *With possession.* ((AUG.)) Elsewhere, *creature.* ((ID.)) Through Christ the Father, etc., *as far as* yet the wood was given, upon which we might sail across.

*This great sea,* etc. ((CASS.)) The second part, where he says: How he leads the Church across the sea of this world to the shore of the homeland. *Creeping things,* etc. ((AUG.)) Evil spirits, whose snares creep.

*This dragon which thou hast formed.* ((ID.)) Besides these animals, etc., *as far as* he was made greater in malice. *For mocking.* ((ID.)) It is said in Job *(Job XL)* that Satan is mocked by the angels of God, who are set over the powers of the air, that they may not hurt us.

*Meat.* ((ID.)) The dragon's food is earth, because it was said to him: *Thou shalt eat earth all the days of my life ((Gen. III))*. Because they that love earthly things are the devil's food. But the food of the just man is the word of God, whence, *Not in bread alone doth man live, but in every word that proceedeth from the mouth of God ((Deut. VIII))*.
*Thy hand, all things shall be filled with good.* ((CASS.)) Or the hand is the power which abundantly fills all things.

*But when thou turnest away.* ((AUG.)) Many, being filled with good, have ascribed it to themselves; but God, willing to prove to them that they have it not from themselves but from God, so that with the good they may have humility, sometimes troubles them, turns away his face, and they fall into temptation.
*Send forth thy spirit.* ((CASS.)) The dust is called theirs, because from themselves they have it that they are dust. But the Spirit is the Lord's: behold the medicine for those returned into dust.

*To tremble.* ((AUG.)) Better is the trembling of humility than the confidence of pride. Whence the Apostle: *With trembling work out your salvation ((Phil. II))*. *The mountains.* ((ID.)) Those who were proud, boasting that all things came from themselves. Even as it happened on mount Sina.

*I will sing.* ((CASS.)) The third part, where he promises that he will sing always. As if he should say: These foretold things the Lord has done, and these being beheld. *In my life.* ((AUG.)) Present and to come; of hope and of sight. Now hope is our life, afterwards it shall be eternal. The life of mortal life is the hope of immortal life. *As long as I am.* ((ID.)) Because in him I am without end, I will sing psalms as long as I am, lest any other act of that life be supposed than to sing psalms: because he who is praised cannot come to be wearisome, it does not become wearisome to praise him; but he is ever loved, ever praised.

*Let it be pleasant.* Another reading: *Let my disputation be sweet to him.* ((AUG.)) For the disputation of man with God is the confession of sins. Whence Isaiah ((Isa. I)). *Take away the wickednesses from your souls, say ye to do well, judge for the fatherless, and come and let us dispute, saith the Lord.* Thy disputation, therefore, is the sacrifice of thy humility, which is sweet to God.
*Bless the Lord, O my soul.* ((ID.)) He repeats what stood at the beginning of the psalm: *Bless the Lord, O my soul,* hinting by this that the end of good men is like the beginning.

notes.text: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God — In all the ways of righteousness. They are the sons of God - Here St. Paul enters upon the description of those blessings which he comprises, ver. 30, in the word glorified; though, indeed, he does not describe mere glory, but that which is still mingled with the cross. The sum is, through sufferings to glory.

For ye — Who are real Christians. Have not received the spirit of bondage - The Holy Ghost was not properly a spirit of bondage, even in the time of the Old Testament. Yet there was something of bondage remaining even in those who then had received the Spirit. Again - As the Jews did before. We - All and every believer. Cry - The word denotes a vehement speaking, with desire, confidence, constancy. Abba, Father - The latter word explains the former. By using both the Syriac and the Greek word, St. Paul seems to point out the joint cry both of the Jewish and gentile believers. The spirit of bondage here seems directly to mean, those operations of the Holy Spirit by which the soul, on its first conviction, feels itself in bondage to sin, to the world, to Satan, and obnoxious to the wrath of God. This, therefore, and the Spirit of adoption, are one and the same Spirit, only manifesting itself in various operations, according to the various circumstances of the persons.

The same Spirit beareth witness with our spirit — With the spirit of every true believer, by a testimony distinct from that of his own spirit, or the testimony of a good conscience. Happy they who enjoy this clear and constant.

Joint heirs — That we may know it is a great inheritance which God will give us for he hath given a great one to his Son. If we suffer with him - Willingly and cheerfully, for righteousness' sake. This is a new proposition, referring to what follows.

glossa.text:
*They are driven.* He says they are driven, not they are ruled. For it is more to be driven than to be ruled: for we say that one is driven, as scarcely doing anything; but that he is ruled, as already doing something, who is therefore ruled that he may act rightly. But they are driven, not because they do nothing of themselves, but because, that they may do something, they are impelled by the force of grace.

((AUG., lib. de Correp. et Grat., c. 2.)) Let them not therefore deceive themselves who say: To what end for us, etc., *as far as* let them rejoice that they have received.

*For you have not received,* etc. You ought to be sons, not servants, because you have not received the spirit of bondage: which makes men serve unwilling through fear of punishment.

*But you have received the spirit of adoption.* It is the same spirit, but because of diverse works it is differently named: he is called the spirit of wrath to the Egyptians, to whom the water divided by the spirit did harm. The son of Israel is not called [a spirit] of wrath, to whom the divided water was of profit. He is the spirit of fear to those who, convicted by the law of their sins and of their own weakness, did not understand the grace of the spirit. He is the spirit of liberty by his working to those to whom regeneration unto life eternal, and faith which works through love, has been imparted. One spirit therefore, which makes two fears. Which also make two kinds of servants. For there is a servant who is also a son, who fears the Lord and honours the father, whence Malachi: *If I am Lord, where is my fear? If father, where is my honour? ((Malach. I))*. And there is a servant who fears punishment, but does not love justice. And because mention is made of fears, it is to be known that besides the natural fear, which is in all, there are four fears, namely: the worldly, which is evil and not from God; and the servile, which is good and from God, but is not sufficient; the initial, which is good and sufficient; and the chaste, which is good and perfecting, of which it is here treated: *For it begets us sons of God. In whom we cry.* This again is from the gift of the Spirit, which makes us so to cry *Abba,* in Hebrew, *father* in Latin. *Abba, father.* Because of the mystery, the Apostle set down both. And in his passion Christ said, *Abba, father,* because the Church is of both peoples, and suffering with her he showed in himself that her sons (the martyrs, namely) ought not to despair, if at the time of passion any sadness from human frailty should creep in.

*That we are the sons of God.* This the Holy Spirit makes us to recognize, while in the Church remission of sins is made; which although the whole Trinity works, yet it is understood to pertain to the Holy Spirit, because he is common to the Father and the Son, and the union of both; through whom is made that fellowship and unity by which we are made one body of the only-begotten Son of God. For unity joins us together, which charity makes, which is not save from the Holy Spirit. These things are said that we may love unity, and fear separation.

*Heirs.* Even though God does not depart, which is spoken according to human laws. Or he will depart, so that he be not seen through a glass in a dark manner as now, but face to face. It can also be said that Christ our head, departing to the passion, left us the possession of ecclesiastical peace, as he himself says: *My peace I give to you, my peace I leave to you ((Joan. XIV))*. Christ also is our inheritance. Whence: *The Lord is the portion of my inheritance ((Psal. XV))*, etc.

*If yet we suffer with him.* To mortify the deeds of the flesh, whence life shall be, no one can without trouble, for which patience is necessary.

notes.text: I am in the Father — The words that I speak, &c. - That is, I am one with the Father, in essence, in speaking, and in acting.
Believe me — On my own word, because I am God. The works - This respects not merely the miracles themselves, but his sovereign, Godlike way of performing them.

Greater works than these shall he do — So one apostle wrought miracles merely by his shadow, Acts v, 15; another by handkerchiefs carried from his body, Acts xix, 12; and all spake with various tongues. But the converting one sinner is a greater work than all these. Because I go to my Father - To send you the Holy Ghost.
If ye love me, keep my commandments — Immediately after faith he exhorts to love and good works.

And I will ask the Father — The 21st verse, ver. 21, shows the connection between this and the preceding verses. And he will give you another Comforter - The Greek word signifies also an advocate, instructer, or encourager. Another - For Christ himself was one. To remain with you forever - With you, and your followers in faith, to the end of the world.

The Spirit of truth — Who has, reveals, testifies, and defends the truth as it is in Jesus. Whom the world - All who do not love or fear God, cannot receive, because it seeth him not - Having no spiritual senses, no internal eye to discern him; nor consequently knoweth him. He shall be in you - As a constant guest. Your bodies and souls shall be temples of the Holy Ghost dwelling in you.

In my name — For my sake, in my room, and as my agent. He will teach you all things - Necessary for you to know. Here is a clear promise to the apostles, and their successors in the faith, that the Holy Ghost will teach them all that truth which is needful for their salvation.

Peace I leave with you — Peace in general; peace with God and with your own consciences. My peace - In particular; that peace which I enjoy, and which I create, I give - At this instant. Not as the world giveth - Unsatisfying unsettled, transient; but filling the soul with constant, even tranquillity. Lord, evermore give us this peace! How serenely may we pass through the most turbulent scenes of life, when all is quiet and harmonious within! Thou hast made peace through the blood of thy cross. May we give all diligence to preserve the inestimable gift inviolate, till it issue in everlasting peace!

glossa.text: *How sayest thou.* And that, when he is wholly like. *How sayest thou,* etc. As if he should say: I see with what mind thou sayest it; thou dost not seek another like me, but thou thinkest [him] better. *Of myself.* Because I who speak am not of myself: he attributes to him what he does, of whom is he himself who does it.

*He that believeth in me.* I and the Father work without difference. And whosoever believes in me (lest this should be taken of the apostles alone), the works that I do through myself, he also shall do, that is, I do in him or through him, and even greater ones. *The works that I do.* Not however of himself, but of me. *The servant is not greater than his lord.* For he himself [does] many things without them, they without him nothing, save sin.

*Greater than these. ((AUG.))* Because if he himself [healed] by the hem of his garment, Peter healed by a shadow. Or his work, etc., *as far as* because if both are of equal power, this is of greater mercy.

*If you love me.* How does he admonish them to love and to keep the commandments, that they may receive the Spirit, whom unless they have they cannot love and keep? But what they had in less measure, secretly, they were to receive more abundantly, openly, so that what they had might become known to them.

*And I will ask the Father. ((THEOPH.))* I will ask, that is, I will beseech the Father, and he will send you another Paraclete, etc., *as far as* that the Paraclete Spirit and his condescending grace may wholly come upon them, he says to them: *I will ask the Father.*

*Because it seeth him not,* etc. The lovers of the world have not spiritual eyes wherewith they might see the Holy Spirit. Nor indeed can they see him with carnal eyes, because the Holy Spirit did not appear clothed in humanity. *And in you.* He shall be in you; he shall not abide in order to be, because to be somewhere is prior to abiding. Let no one therefore think that he so abides as a guest visibly with another; but in them he can be known, not by others.

*These things have I spoken to you.* These things concerning the mansion in those who love him, in which is signified the future spiritual Church, in which are the blessed, from whom he does not withdraw. *Abiding with you.* Here [is] the present bodily Church, in which he visits by delivering, and returns.

*The Paraclete.* Although to console is the work of the Trinity, yet it pertains most of all to the person of the Holy Spirit, because in Scripture the Holy Spirit is designated by the name of goodness: through goodness therefore God consoles us, through it he bestows on us all his good things.

*He you.* Because even though the Son teaches us and reveals the Father, he does all this through his goodness. *He shall teach you all things.* He shall teach the things that I shall have said, not that the Son says and the Spirit teaches, because what he says and teaches, the Trinity itself also says and teaches. But because it is a Trinity, it behoves the single persons to be intimated, whom we ought to hear distinctly, to understand inseparably. When therefore we say, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, we do not say them at the same time, since they cannot be not at the same time.

*Peace I leave with you.* Being about to go to the Father. *Peace,* etc. And repeating concerning the same. *My peace I give.* And this is what the Prophet says: *Peace upon peace ((Isa. XXVII))*. There is a peace in this world, abiding in which we conquer the enemy, love one another, and do not judge one another concerning hidden things. There will be a peace in the world to come when we shall reign without an enemy, where one will not be able to dissent from another, where *all things are open and praise is to each one ((I Cor. IV))*. But in him and from him is each peace. *For he himself is our peace ((Ephes. II))*, and we believe him, because he is, and we shall see him as he is. Whence what he says, my, from the latter is to be understood also of the former. Or, the peace in this world is ours, which is some [peace] and not full; and from him in the world to come is his own peace, where nothing is repugnant, in the manner in which he himself has it.

*Let it not be troubled.* Because I leave you in peace, let not your heart be troubled at that which I said, I go, as though at the shepherd's absence the wolf invades; because as man I go, as God I am present.

echoes.text: On the third day, when it was morning, there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mountain, and the sound of an exceedingly loud trumpet; and all the people who were in the camp trembled. Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God; and they stood at the lower part of the mountain. Mount Sinai, all it, smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire; and its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked […]
echoes.note: The Sinai theophany supplies the dominant template: a sound from heaven, fire descending on the assembly, and the whole 'house' shaken/filled echo the thunder, fire, and trembling mountain when YHWH descended in fire and the trumpet-sound grew loud (Exod 19:16-19). Volume is carried structurally (sound + fire + divine descent on the gathered people) more than by shared vocabulary. Recurrence is strong: Luke repeatedly frames the Spirit's coming as a new covenantal endowment. Thematic coherence is very high, since Pentecost (Weeks) was associated in Second Temple/rabbinic tradition with the Sinai law-giving, making Acts 2 a Spirit-Sinai counterpart. History of interpretation overwhelmingly reads Pentecost as a Sinai antitype.

echoes.text: The whole earth was of one language and of one speech. As they traveled east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and they lived there. They said one to another, “Come, let’s make bricks, and burn them thoroughly.” They had brick for stone, and they used tar for mortar. They said, “Come, let’s build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top reaches to the sky, and let’s make ourselves a name, lest we be scattered abroad on the surface of the whole […]
echoes.note: Babel reversal: at Babel one language is confused and humanity scattered; at Pentecost the Spirit enables many tongues that gather scattered nations into mutual comprehension. Verbal volume is low/absent, but the structural correspondence (languages, scattering vs. ingathering) is a classic typological inversion. Thematic coherence is high given the immediately following nations-list (vv.9-11). Recurrence: Luke's universalizing program (gospel to all nations) reinforces the figure. Widely noted in history of interpretation as the undoing of Babel; the satisfaction of reading it this way is considerable.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions. And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.
echoes.note: The outpouring of the Spirit enacted here is precisely what Peter will name as Joel's prophecy in vv.16-21; the narrative event (all filled with the Spirit, all speaking/prophesying) is the fulfillment Joel foretold of the Spirit poured 'on all flesh.' High thematic coherence and explicit recurrence within the same chapter. Volume in vv.1-4 is event-level rather than verbal, but the link is interpretively certain because Luke makes it explicit a few verses later.

echoes.text: Moses went out, and told the people Yahweh’s words; and he gathered seventy men of the elders of the people, and set them around the Tent. Yahweh came down in the cloud, and spoke to him, and took of the Spirit that was on him, and put it on the seventy elders. When the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but they did so no more. But two men remained in the camp. The name of one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the Spirit rested on […]
echoes.note: When the Spirit rests on the seventy elders they prophesy, and Moses wishes 'that all the LORD's people were prophets, that the LORD would put his Spirit on them.' Acts 2 reads as the realization of that wish: the Spirit democratized onto the whole community, who immediately prophesy/speak. Moderate volume (shared motif of Spirit-induced prophecy distributed across many), strong thematic coherence, recurrence via Joel which itself develops the Numbers ideal.

echoes.text: He said, “Go out, and stand on the mountain before Yahweh.” Behold, Yahweh passed by, and a great and strong wind tore the mountains, and broke in pieces the rocks before Yahweh; but Yahweh was not in the wind. After the wind an earthquake; but Yahweh was not in the earthquake. After the earthquake a fire passed; but Yahweh was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.
echoes.note: Elijah's Horeb theophany pairs wind and fire as accompaniments of divine presence, a constellation reused here (wind-like sound, fire-like tongues). Faint, carried by shared theophanic imagery rather than wording; contested because the Sinai/Exodus material is the more direct source and the elements function differently (there God is not in the wind/fire).

echoes.text: Then he said to me, Prophesy to the wind, prophesy, son of man, and tell the wind, Thus says the Lord Yahweh: Come from the four winds, breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live. So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up on their feet, an exceedingly great army. Then he said to me, Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel: behold, they say, Our bones are dried up, and our hope […]
echoes.note: The life-giving rûaḥ/breath/wind that comes and animates the people resonates with the wind-like sound that fills the house and empowers the disciples. Low verbal volume in the Greek, but the Spirit-as-wind giving new life is thematically coherent with the inauguration of the renewed community; contested as a deliberate echo.

echoes.text: Now this is the history of the generations of the sons of Noah and of Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Sons were born to them after the flood. The sons of Japheth were: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras. The sons of Gomer were: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah. The sons of Javan were: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim. Of these were the islands of the nations divided in their lands, everyone after his language, after their families, in […]
echoes.note: The roll-call of peoples 'from every nation under heaven' (Parthians, Medes, Elamites, etc., vv.9-11) functions as a New Testament Table of Nations, recalling the Genesis 10 enumeration of the descendants of Noah scattered across the earth. The motif of representative nations gathered echoes the primeval mapping of humanity; thematic coherence high, verbal overlap modest (proper-name catalogue form). Pairs with the Babel figure of vv.1-4.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions. And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.
echoes.note: The crowd's marveling that each hears the disciples 'speaking in our own tongues the mighty works of God' realizes Joel's promised universal prophesying poured out on all flesh; the mockery of drunkenness (v.13) sets up Peter's Joel citation directly. Recurrence within the chapter is explicit; thematic coherence high.

echoes.text: This day will I begin to put the dread of you and the fear of you on the peoples who are under the whole sky, who shall hear the report of you, and shall tremble, and be in anguish because of you.”
echoes.note: The phrase 'peoples under the whole heaven' supplies the universalizing idiom behind 'every nation under heaven' (v.5). Faint, formulaic; contested as a specific source since the expression is common LXX phrasing.

echoes.text: It will happen in that day that the Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea. He will set up a banner for the nations, and will assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
echoes.note: Isaiah's eschatological ingathering of the dispersed of Israel/Judah from Egypt, Cush, Elam, Shinar, and the coastlands anticipates the gathering of diaspora Jews 'from every nation' to Jerusalem. The geographic spread of the returnees parallels the list of nations here. Low volume, plausible thematic coherence with a restoration-of-the-dispersed reading; contested.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions. And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit. I will show wonders in the heavens and in the earth: blood, fire, and pillars of smoke. The sun will be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day […]
echoes.note: Formal, formula-marked citation ('this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel,' v.16) reproducing Joel 2:28-32 (LXX 3:1-5) at high verbal volume: pouring out the Spirit on all flesh, sons/daughters prophesying, young men visions, old men dreams, servants and handmaids, wonders in heaven and signs on earth, blood/fire/smoke, sun to darkness and moon to blood before the great day of the Lord, and whoever calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved. Luke's 'in the last days' adapts Joel's 'afterward.' The anchor quotation of the chapter; maximal on all three auditable tests.

echoes.text: Mount Sinai, all it, smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire; and its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked greatly.
echoes.note: The 'smoke' (kapnos) among the apocalyptic signs (v.19) may resonate with the smoke of Sinai where 'the mountain was wholly in smoke' at the theophany, reinforcing the Sinai-Pentecost frame. Low volume and the wording is governed by Joel; contested.

echoes.text: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and terrible day of Yahweh comes.
echoes.note: 'Before the great and notable day of the Lord' overlaps the Malachi expectation of the great and dreadful day of the LORD; the phrase is shared eschatological idiom that Joel and Malachi both carry. Faint and mediated through Joel; contested as an independent source.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

places.name: Jerusalem
places.id: The City of David and Old City, on the spurs above the Kidron Valley, c. 50 km from the Mediterranean. Pre-Israelite Jebus; named here as the seat of Adoni-Zedek, leader of the southern coalition.

places.name: Judea
places.id: The Roman administrative province (later procuratorial province) covering the southern hill country of Israel — Jerusalem, the Judean wilderness, and territory south to the Negev. The Greco-Roman successor to the Hasmonean and Herodian Iudaea. Pin sits in the central hill country.

places.name: Parthia
places.id: The empire stretching from the Euphrates eastward across the Iranian plateau under the Arsacid dynasty (247 B.C. – A.D. 224). Rome's principal eastern rival in the apostolic period. Pin sits in the Parthian heartland near Hecatompylos / Damghan.

places.name: Media
places.id: The northwestern Iranian plateau, capital at Ecbatana (modern Hamadan). By the apostolic period a satrapy of the Parthian empire. The Medes appear as a distinct people in Acts 2 even though their kingdom had been absorbed centuries earlier.

places.name: Elam
places.id: The lowland region of southwestern Iran (Khuzestan), traditionally centered on Susa. By the first century the Hellenistic Susiana, governed under Parthian overlordship.

places.name: Mesopotamia
places.id: The land between the Tigris and Euphrates. In the apostolic period split between Roman client kingdoms in the upper basin (Edessa) and Parthian control of Babylonia. Pin sits in the middle Euphrates region.

places.name: Cappadocia
places.id: The interior Anatolian plateau, made a Roman province under Tiberius in A.D. 17. Famous in late antiquity for its volcanic-tuff landscape and rock-hewn churches; in the first century a primarily rural province with a mixed Hellenistic and Iranian-influenced elite.

places.name: Pontus
places.id: The Black Sea coast of northern Anatolia, the kingdom of Mithridates VI in the late Hellenistic period, partitioned into a Roman province and client states after 63 B.C. The home region of Aquila (Acts 18:2).

places.name: Asia
places.id: The Roman province (formed 129 B.C.) covering the western third of Anatolia, with Ephesus as its capital and the seven cities of Revelation 1-3 within its bounds. Distinct from 'Asia' as a continent and from the Seleucid use of the term for the wider Anatolian-Syrian sphere.

places.name: Phrygia
places.id: The west-central Anatolian plateau, a cultural region split administratively between Roman Asia (west) and Galatia (east) in the apostolic period. Pisidian Antioch and Iconium lay within the wider Phrygian zone.

places.name: Pamphylia
places.id: The narrow coastal plain of southern Anatolia between Lycia (west) and Cilicia (east), with Perga and Attalia as its principal cities. A Roman province (combined with Lycia under Vespasian).

places.name: Egypt
places.id: The Nile valley civilization, the land of Israel's bondage. Pin sits on the Nile near ancient Memphis.

places.name: Libya
places.id: The Roman province of Cyrenaica (later Libya superior), the coastal strip of north Africa west of Egypt. The phrase 'parts of Libya around Cyrene' in Acts 2:10 picks out the Pentapolis region around the city.

places.name: Cyrene
places.id: The chief Greek city of the Cyrenaican coast (modern Shahhat, Libya). A major Jewish community is attested in the apostolic period; Simon of Cyrene was conscripted to bear Jesus' cross (Mk 15:21).

places.name: Rome
places.id: The imperial capital. In Acts the city is the goal of Paul's career (1:8 'to the uttermost parts of the earth'; 19:21; 28:14-16) and the destination of his appeal to Caesar.

places.name: Crete
places.id: The largest of the Greek islands, a Roman province (combined with Cyrene) since 67 B.C. Paul's voyage to Rome touches the south coast at Fair Havens and Phoenix (Acts 27).

places.name: Arabia
places.id: In the New Testament principally the Nabataean kingdom east of the Jordan and the Dead Sea, with Petra as its capital — annexed as Roman Arabia in A.D. 106. Pin sits at Petra. Paul's 'three years in Arabia' of Gal 1:17 places him in this kingdom rather than the wider peninsula.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: You shall tell Pharaoh, ‘Thus says Yahweh, Israel is my son, my firstborn, and I have said to you, “Let my son go, that he may serve me”; and you have refused to let him go. Behold, I will kill your son, your firstborn.’”
echoes.note: 'Israel is my son, my firstborn' grounds the sonship/adoption language of vv.14-17; the Spirit constitutes believers as 'children of God,' transferring Israel's sonship status to those led by the Spirit.

echoes.text: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says Yahweh: I will put my law in their inward parts, and in their heart will I write it; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people:
echoes.note: The Spirit enabling 'the ordinance of the law' to be 'fulfilled in us' (v.4) draws on the new-covenant promise to write the Torah on the heart, internalizing the law by divine agency rather than external command.

echoes.text: I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my ordinances, and do them.
echoes.note: 'I will put my Spirit within you and cause you to walk in my statutes' undergirds vv.4-9: the indwelling Spirit (vv.9,11) produces obedience and 'walking according to the Spirit'; the verbal cluster Spirit-indwelling-walking-statutes is distinctive to Ezekiel.

echoes.text: I will put my Spirit in you, and you shall live, and I will place you in your own land: and you shall know that I, Yahweh, have spoken it and performed it, says Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'I will put my Spirit in you and you shall live' (the dry-bones vision) lies behind v.11, where the Spirit who raised Jesus 'will also give life to your mortal bodies'; Spirit-giving-life-to-dead-bodies is the precise Ezekielian figure.

echoes.text: Behold, I have set before you this day life and prosperity, and death and evil. For I command you this day to love Yahweh your God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments, his statutes, and his ordinances, that you may live and multiply, and that Yahweh your God may bless you in the land where you go in to possess it. But if your heart turns away, and you will not hear, but are drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them; I denounce to […]
echoes.note: 'The mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace' and 'if you live after the flesh you must die... by the Spirit... you will live' (vv.6,13) reframe the covenantal life-and-death choice of Moses' exhortation set before Israel.

echoes.text: “When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.
echoes.note: 'When Israel was a child I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son' supplies the adopted-son-led-by-God motif (vv.14-15); the tender father-son relation undergirds the cry 'Abba! Father!'

echoes.text: Yet the number of the children of Israel will be as the sand of the sea, which can’t be measured nor numbered; and it will come to pass that, in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not my people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’
echoes.note: 'In the place where it was said to them, You are not my people, it shall be said, You are children of the living God' anticipates 'these are children of God' / 'we are children of God' (vv.14,16); Paul cites this very text in Romans 9:26.

echoes.text: if the anointed priest sins so as to bring guilt on the people, then let him offer for his sin, which he has sinned, a young bull without defect to Yahweh for a sin offering.
echoes.note: 'for sin' (peri hamartias) in v.3 reproduces the Septuagint's standing phrase for the sin offering; God's sending his Son 'for sin' figurally casts Christ in the role of the Levitical purification sacrifice that 'condemns sin in the flesh.'

echoes.text: Yahweh said, “My Spirit will not strive with man forever, because he also is flesh; so his days will be one hundred twenty years.”
echoes.note: The flesh/Spirit antithesis (vv.5-9), where 'flesh' marks mortal humanity opposed to God's enduring Spirit, faintly recalls 'My Spirit will not abide in man forever, for he is flesh.'

echoes.text: Yahweh God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
echoes.note: 'The spirit is alive' / God giving 'life to your mortal bodies' (vv.10-11) faintly evokes the breath of life animating dust-formed Adam, now reapplied as resurrection-life by the Spirit.

echoes.text: For you are our Father, though Abraham doesn’t know us, and Israel does not acknowledge us: you, Yahweh, are our Father; our Redeemer from everlasting is your name.
echoes.note: 'You, O LORD, are our Father' — Israel's corporate address of God as Father — stands behind the Spirit-prompted filial cry 'Abba! Father!' (v.15).

echoes.text: “But I said, ‘How I would put you among the children, and give you a pleasant land, a goodly heritage of the armies of the nations!’ and I said, ‘You shall call me “My Father”, and shall not turn away from following me.’
echoes.note: 'I thought you would call me My Father and would not turn from following me' — God's hope that adopted Israel address him as Father — resonates with the adoptive cry of v.15.

echoes.text: I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you will be my people.
echoes.note: The covenant formula 'I will... be your God, and you shall be my people,' realized through the indwelling Spirit (vv.9-16), faintly underlies the divine-belonging and sonship affirmed by the Spirit's testimony.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: He said, “Please show me your glory.” He said, “I will make all my goodness pass before you, and will proclaim Yahweh’s name before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.” He said, “You cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.” Yahweh also said, “Behold, there is a place by me, and you shall stand on the rock. It will happen, while my glory passes by, that I will put you in a cleft of […]
echoes.note: Philip's 'show us the Father' directly replays Moses' 'show me your glory,' to which God replies that no one can see his face and live. John inverts the denial: the one who has seen Jesus has seen the Father, fulfilling the Sinai longing to behold God. High Volume and Coherence given the explicit 'show us'/'show me' request and John's programmatic 'no one has ever seen God; the only Son has made him known' (1:18).

echoes.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. He turned again into the camp, but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, didn’t depart from the Tent.
echoes.note: The LORD spoke to Moses 'face to face, as a man speaks to his friend,' yet 33:20 forbids seeing God's face directly; this tension is exactly what 14:9 resolves by locating the Father's visible presence in Jesus. Coherence with the surrounding Exodus 33 theophany strengthens the medium rating beyond the headline 33:18-23 allusion.

echoes.text: Yahweh spoke to you out of the midst of the fire: you heard the voice of words, but you saw no form; you only heard a voice.
echoes.note: At Horeb Israel 'heard the sound of words but saw no form,' codifying that God is heard, not seen. Jesus' claim that his words are the Father's and that seeing him is seeing the Father answers this aniconic tradition. Low confidence: thematic counterpoint rather than verbal echo, supporting the 'unseen God' frame behind the pericope.

echoes.text: I will raise them up a prophet from among their brothers, like you. I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I shall command him.
echoes.note: God promises a prophet 'in whose mouth I will put my words... he shall speak all that I command him,' the pattern Jesus claims in 14:10: 'the words I speak are not from myself; the Father does his works.' The prophet-like-Moses speech-formula gives modest Coherence with John's sent-one Christology; low because John does not cite the prophet text here.

echoes.text: With him, I will speak mouth to mouth, even plainly, and not in riddles; and he shall see Yahweh’s form. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant, against Moses?”
echoes.note: Moses uniquely beholds 'the form of the LORD' and speaks with him 'mouth to mouth,' a near-vision that 14:9 surpasses by granting the disciples the Father in the Son. Faint, contested support for the seeing-God motif; the lexical overlap is limited to the shared theophanic register.

echoes.text: but your eyes have seen all of Yahweh’s great work which he did.
echoes.note: Israel had 'seen all the great work of the LORD that he did,' framing God's redemptive deeds as 'works' the people witness; Jesus speaks of 'the works that I do' continuing in his followers. Low confidence: 'works of the LORD' is a broad Deuteronomic idiom rather than a targeted source, offering only thematic coloring to 14:12.

echoes.text: Israel served Yahweh all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua, and had known all the work of Yahweh, that he had worked for Israel.
echoes.note: Israel served the LORD all the days that the elders 'had known all the work of the LORD that he did for Israel,' another instance of redemptive deeds as 'works.' It reinforces the OT 'works of God' register behind Jesus' 'greater works,' but is too generic to credit as a specific allusion; flagged low and contested.

echoes.text: Yahweh, you will ordain peace for us, for you have also worked all our works for us.
echoes.note: 'You have indeed done all our works for us,' confessing that human works are wrought by God, resonates faintly with 14:12's promise that believers will do the works Jesus does because he goes to the Father. Low and contested: a thematic affinity about divinely-empowered works rather than a deliberate citation.

echoes.text: Yahweh is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth. He will fulfill the desire of those who fear him. He also will hear their cry, and will save them.
echoes.note: 'The LORD is near to all who call on him... he fulfills the desire of those who fear him' undergirds the answered-petition promise of 14:13-14 ('whatever you ask in my name'). The granting-of-requests motif is widespread in the Psalter; low confidence because no single verse is verbally anchored, though it situates Jesus in the role of the request-granting LORD.

echoes.text: I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my ordinances, and do them.
echoes.note: 'I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes' supplies the new-covenant gift of an indwelling Spirit that produces obedience, exactly the logic of 14:15-17 where loving-and-obeying flows into the Paraclete who 'will be in you.' High Coherence: the Spirit given to dwell within and to enable commandment-keeping is Ezekiel's signature promise.

echoes.text: You shall love Yahweh your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.
echoes.note: The Shema's command to 'love the LORD your God' grounds the love-of-God demanded in 14:15, now reoriented to Jesus: 'if you love me, keep my commandments.' Coherence is strong because John fuses love and obedience in the Deuteronomic manner; medium rather than high since the wording is paraphrased and reattributed to Jesus.

echoes.text: Know therefore that Yahweh your God himself is God, the faithful God, who keeps covenant and loving kindness with them who love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations,
echoes.note: God keeps covenant 'with those who love him and keep his commandments,' the precise love+keep-commandments pairing echoed in 14:15 and 14:21. Recurrence of this formula across Deuteronomy raises Volume; the contestation is that John supplies the idiom without a citation marker.

echoes.text: and showing loving kindness to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.
echoes.note: The Decalogue promises steadfast love 'to those who love me and keep my commandments,' the foundational love-and-obey formula behind 14:15. Strong Coherence with John's repeated linkage of loving Jesus and keeping his word; medium because it is one of several overlapping Pentateuchal sources for the same idiom.

echoes.text: The Spirit of Yahweh will rest on him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'The Spirit of the LORD shall rest on him, the Spirit of wisdom... and of knowledge' anchors the messianic 'Spirit of truth' the Father gives in 14:17. Coherence is good because Isaiah's endowing Spirit is a Spirit of knowledge/truth resting permanently; medium given the conceptual rather than verbal link to 'Spirit of truth.'

echoes.text: But they rebelled, and grieved his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he himself fought against them. Then he remembered the days of old, Moses and his people, saying, Where is he who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of his flock? where is he who put his holy Spirit in their midst?
echoes.note: Israel 'grieved his Holy Spirit,' yet God 'put in the midst of them his Holy Spirit,' one of the rare OT uses of 'his Holy Spirit' that the Paraclete passages presuppose. The motif of God placing his Spirit among the people undergirds 14:16-17's abiding Counselor; medium for the shared 'Holy Spirit' terminology with the wider Isaianic-Spirit complex.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions. And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.
echoes.note: 'I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh' is the eschatological Spirit-bestowal that 14:16-17 promises in personalized form as the indwelling Paraclete. Coherence is solid within John's realized-eschatology of the Spirit's coming; medium because John individualizes the corporate outpouring and offers no verbal quotation.

echoes.text: This is the word that I covenanted with you when you came out of Egypt, and my Spirit lived among you. ‘Don’t be afraid.’
echoes.note: 'My Spirit remains in your midst; do not fear' couples the abiding Spirit with the dismissal of fear, paralleling the Paraclete who abides 'forever' alongside 14:27's 'let not your heart be afraid.' Low confidence: a suggestive thematic pairing of abiding-Spirit and courage rather than a demonstrable citation.

echoes.text: Yahweh came down in the cloud, and spoke to him, and took of the Spirit that was on him, and put it on the seventy elders. When the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but they did so no more. But two men remained in the camp. The name of one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the Spirit rested on them; and they were of those who were written, but had not gone out to the Tent; and they prophesied in the camp. A young man ran, and told […]
echoes.note: The LORD takes the Spirit on Moses and places it on the seventy, with Moses wishing all the LORD's people were prophets endowed with the Spirit. This distribution of the Spirit to the community prefigures the Paraclete given to all the disciples; low and contested because the link is conceptual, lacking the 'Spirit of truth' vocabulary.

echoes.text: For a holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit. And will start away from thoughts that are without understanding, And will be put to confusion when unrighteousness has come in.
echoes.note: 'A holy and disciplined spirit will flee from deceit' and (1:7) 'the Spirit of the Lord has filled the world' offer a Second-Temple 'spirit of truth/wisdom that the deceitful world cannot hold,' resonant with 14:17's Spirit 'whom the world cannot receive.' Low confidence: deuterocanonical mood-music supporting the truth-vs-world contrast rather than a direct source.

harmony.note: Five chapters where the Synoptics give the meal: the new commandment, the vine, the Paraclete, and the high-priestly prayer. John only.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Come, Holy Spirit,
the fire of God, the breath of life.
A sound like a rushing wind filled the house, and tongues of flame rested on each of them,
and they spoke of God's deeds in every language under heaven.
You send forth your Spirit, and the face of the earth is made new;
the Spirit cries within us, Abba, Father.
Come, Holy Spirit.
May we feel God's fire through our worship.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Wait in the upstairs room with the doors shut and the morning quiet, and then — a sound, far off and coming closer, like a great wind.
Come, Holy Spirit, the fire of God, the breath of life!
It fills the whole house, and over each head a small tongue of flame comes to rest, and no one is left untouched.
Come, Holy Spirit, the fire of God, the breath of life!
The doors fly open and they spill into the street, and every traveler hears the wonders of God in their own mother tongue.
Come, Holy Spirit, the fire of God, the breath of life!
You send out your breath and the dust comes alive; you renew the face of the whole tired earth.
Come, Holy Spirit, the fire of God, the breath of life!
So fall on us again, Spirit of truth and comfort, and teach us to cry: Abba, Father.
Come, Holy Spirit, the fire of God, the breath of life!

lines: A rushing wind fills the house; flame rests on every head.
Come, Holy Spirit, the fire of God, the breath of life!
They spill into the street, and every language hears the wonders of God.
Come, Holy Spirit, the fire of God, the breath of life!
You send your breath, and the face of the earth is made new.
Come, Holy Spirit, the fire of God, the breath of life!
Teach us to cry, Abba, Father; come, let us worship.
Come, Holy Spirit, the fire of God, the breath of life!
